struct mg_timer {
  uint64_t period_ms;          // Timer period in milliseconds
  uint64_t expire;             // Expiration timestamp in milliseconds
  unsigned flags;              // Possible flags values below
#define MG_TIMER_ONCE 0        // Call function once
#define MG_TIMER_REPEAT 1      // Call function periodically
#define MG_TIMER_RUN_NOW 2     // Call immediately when timer is set
#define MG_TIMER_CALLED 4      // Timer function was called at least once
#define MG_TIMER_AUTODELETE 8  // mg_free() timer when done
  void (*fn)(void *);          // Function to call
  void *arg;                   // Function argument
  struct mg_timer *next;       // Linkage
};

struct mg_connection {
  struct mg_connection *next;     // Linkage in struct mg_mgr :: connections
  struct mg_mgr *mgr;             // Our container
  struct mg_addr loc;             // Local address
  struct mg_addr rem;             // Remote address
  void *fd;                       // Connected socket, or LWIP data
  unsigned long id;               // Auto-incrementing unique connection ID
  struct mg_iobuf recv;           // Incoming data
  struct mg_iobuf send;           // Outgoing data
  struct mg_iobuf prof;           // Profile data enabled by MG_ENABLE_PROFILE
  struct mg_iobuf rtls;           // TLS only. Incoming encrypted data
  mg_event_handler_t fn;          // User-specified event handler function
  void *fn_data;                  // User-specified function parameter
  mg_event_handler_t pfn;         // Protocol-specific handler function
  void *pfn_data;                 // Protocol-specific function parameter
  char data[MG_DATA_SIZE];        // Arbitrary connection data
  void *tls;                      // TLS specific data
  unsigned is_listening : 1;      // Listening connection
  unsigned is_client : 1;         // Outbound (client) connection
  unsigned is_accepted : 1;       // Accepted (server) connection
  unsigned is_resolving : 1;      // Non-blocking DNS resolution is in progress
  unsigned is_arplooking : 1;     // Non-blocking ARP resolution is in progress
  unsigned is_connecting : 1;     // Non-blocking connect is in progress
  unsigned is_tls : 1;            // TLS-enabled connection
  unsigned is_tls_hs : 1;         // TLS handshake is in progress
  unsigned is_udp : 1;            // UDP connection
  unsigned is_websocket : 1;      // WebSocket connection
  unsigned is_mqtt5 : 1;          // For MQTT connection, v5 indicator
  unsigned is_hexdumping : 1;     // Hexdump in/out traffic
  unsigned is_draining : 1;       // Send remaining data, then close and free
  unsigned is_closing : 1;        // Close and free the connection immediately
  unsigned is_full : 1;           // Stop reads, until cleared
  unsigned is_tls_throttled : 1;  // Last TLS write: MG_SOCK_PENDING() was true
  unsigned is_resp : 1;           // Response is still being generated
  unsigned is_readable : 1;       // Connection is ready to read
  unsigned is_writable : 1;       // Connection is ready to write
};

functions.name: mg_str

Input must point to a readable NUL-terminated string.

functions.name: mg_str_n

functions.description: Create an mg_str from a memory buffer of known length n.
requirements: s may be NULL only if n == 0.
Buffer s must be readable for at least n bytes.

functions.name: mg_casecmp
functions.signature: int mg_casecmp(const char *s1, const char *s2);
functions.description: Case-insensitive comparison of two C strings, similar to strcasecmp.
requirements: s1 and s2 must be NUL-terminated strings.
Pointers must be non-NULL.

functions.name: mg_strcmp
functions.signature: int mg_strcmp(const struct mg_str str1, const struct mg_str str2);

functions.name: mg_strcasecmp

functions.description: Case-insensitive comparison of two mg_str values.
requirements: Buffers must be readable for their lengths.

s.buf must be readable for s.len bytes.

functions.name: mg_match

functions.description: Match str against pattern (likely glob/wildcard); optionally capture submatches into caps.

caps may be NULL if captures are not needed; if provided, it must point to sufficient storage as expected by implementation.
Pattern syntax details are not documented here (unknown).

functions.name: mg_span
functions.signature: bool mg_span(struct mg_str s, struct mg_str *a, struct mg_str *b, char delim);

a and b must be non-NULL pointers to receive results.

functions.description: Parse an mg_str into an integer of a given base and store into val buffer of size val_len.

functions.name: mg_queue_init

Second argument must be a writable buffer; size is total capacity.
Caller must ensure SPSC access semantics.

functions.name: mg_queue_book
functions.signature: size_t mg_queue_book(struct mg_queue *, char **buf, size_t);

buf must be a valid pointer to receive the reserved region pointer.
Requested size must fit in available space.

functions.name: mg_queue_add

functions.name: mg_queue_next
functions.signature: size_t mg_queue_next(struct mg_queue *, char **);
functions.description: Get the pointer and size of the oldest message in the queue without removing it.
requirements: Queue must be initialized.
Output pointer must be non-NULL.

functions.name: mg_queue_del
functions.signature: void mg_queue_del(struct mg_queue *, size_t);
functions.description: Delete (consume) the oldest message from the queue by size.
requirements: Size must match the size returned by last mg_queue_next.

import random
import struct
import zlib

# Generator for arbitrary binary data tailored to exercise many code paths that
# accept length-delimited buffers (e.g., mg_str with explicit len, HTTP/JSON,
# Base64/hex, URL encode/decode, MQTT/DNS/SNTP parsers). The goal is to return
# a single bytes buffer that stubs will slice or interpret in different ways via
# FUZZ_PARAM_STR / FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME.

ASCII = [
    b"", b"a", b"A", b"0", b" ", b"\t", b"\n", b"\r",
    b"/", b"?", b"&", b"=", b"+", b"%", b"-", b"_", b".", b",",
]

def _rand_bytes(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))

def _rand_ascii(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    alphabet = b"abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789-_.:/?&=%+ \t\r\n"
    return bytes(alphabet[rng.randrange(len(alphabet))] for _ in range(n))

def _http_request(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Build a small, well-formed HTTP request with headers and body
    methods = [b"GET", b"POST", b"PUT", b"DELETE", b"PATCH", b"OPTIONS"]
    paths = [b"/", b"/index.html", b"/api/v1/resource", b"/upload", b"/a%20b?q=1&x=y"]
    method = rng.choice(methods)
    path = rng.choice(paths)
    proto = b"HTTP/1.1"
    host = b"example.com"
    headers = [
        b"Host: " + host,
        b"User-Agent: fuzzgen/1.0",
        b"Accept: */*",
        b"Cookie: a=1; b=two; c=three",
        b"Authorization: Basic dXNlcjpwYXNz",
    ]
    body = b""
    if method in (b"POST", b"PUT", b"PATCH"):
        # Randomly choose simple forms or JSON
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            body = b"name=John+Doe&age=42&note=hello%20world"
            headers.append(b"Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded")
        else:
            body = b'{"id":123,"ok":true,"pi":3.14,"arr":[1,2,3],"hex":"deadbeef","b64":"Zm9vYmFy"}'
            headers.append(b"Content-Type: application/json")
        headers.append(b"Content-Length: " + str(len(body)).encode())
    req = method + b" " + path + b" " + proto + b"\r\n" + b"\r\n".join(headers) + b"\r\n\r\n" + body
    return req

def _http_response(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    status = rng.choice([b"200 OK", b"204 No Content", b"301 Moved Permanently", b"400 Bad Request", b"500 Internal Server Error"])  # noqa: E501
    proto = b"HTTP/1.1"
    headers = [
        b"Server: mg",
        b"Content-Type: text/plain",
    ]
    body = b"Hello, world!\n"
    headers.append(b"Content-Length: " + str(len(body)).encode())
    return proto + b" " + status + b"\r\n" + b"\r\n".join(headers) + b"\r\n\r\n" + body

def _json_doc(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # JSON with varied types and nested objects/arrays
    samples = [
        b'{"a":1,"b":true,"c":"str","d":null}',
        b'{"user":{"name":"Alice","age":30},"ok":false,"arr":[10,20,30]}',
        b'{"hex":"0123abcd","b64":"QUJDREVGRw==","num":-42,"f":2.5}',
        b'[{"k":"v"}, {"x":1}, 3, true, null]'
    ]
    return rng.choice(samples)

def _base64_blob(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Include raw + base64-ish text
    raw = _rand_bytes(rng, rng.randint(8, 64))
    b64chars = b"ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789+/="
    b64 = bytes(b64chars[rng.randrange(len(b64chars))] for _ in range(rng.randint(12, 96)))
    return raw + b"\n" + b64 + b"\n"

def _dns_like_packet(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Minimal DNS header (12 bytes) followed by random payload
    txnid = rng.randrange(0, 65536)
    flags = rng.randrange(0, 65536)
    qdcount = rng.randrange(0, 2)
    ancount = rng.randrange(0, 2)
    nscount = 0
    arcount = 0
    hdr = struct.pack("!6H", txnid, flags, qdcount, ancount, nscount, arcount)
    rest = _rand_bytes(rng, rng.randint(0, 64))
    return hdr + rest

def _sntp_like_packet(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # 48 bytes SNTP minimum, fill with semi-sane values
    buf = bytearray(48)
    buf[0] = 0x1b  # LI=0, VN=3, Mode=3 (client)
    # Transmit Timestamp seconds (random epoch near 2020..2030)
    # SNTP uses NTP epoch (1900). We'll just randomize bytes.
    for i in range(40, 48):
        buf[i] = rng.getrandbits(8)
    return bytes(buf)

def _mqtt_like(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Simple PUBLISH-like: fixed header + remaining length + topic + payload
    topic = rng.choice([b"a/b", b"home/room1/temp", b"test"])  # small
    payload = _rand_ascii(rng, rng.randint(0, 64))
    # Fixed header: PUBLISH (0x30), flags random retain/qos
    flags = rng.randrange(0, 0x10)
    fixed = bytes([0x30 | (flags & 0x0F)])
    var = topic
    rl = len(var) + len(payload) + 2  # 2 bytes for topic length
    # MQTT remaining length variable encoding
    rem = bytearray()
    x = rl
    while True:
        byte = x % 128
        x //= 128
        if x > 0:
            byte |= 0x80
        rem.append(byte)
        if x == 0:
            break
    pkt = fixed + bytes(rem) + struct.pack("!H", len(topic)) + topic + payload
    return pkt

def _urlish(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    schemes = [b"http", b"https", b"ws", b"wss", b"mqtt", b"sntp"]
    host = rng.choice([b"localhost", b"127.0.0.1", b"[::1]", b"example.com"]) 
    port = b":" + str(rng.randrange(1, 65535)).encode() if rng.random() < 0.5 else b""
    path = rng.choice([b"/", b"/a", b"/x/y", b"/api?q=1&x=2", b"/ws#frag"]) 
    return rng.choice(schemes) + b"://" + host + port + path

def _multipart_form(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    boundary = b"----fuzzboundary" + _rand_ascii(rng, 6)
    parts = []
    parts.append(b"--" + boundary + b"\r\nContent-Disposition: form-data; name=\"field\"\r\n\r\nvalue\r\n")
    parts.append(b"--" + boundary + b"\r\nContent-Disposition: form-data; name=\"file\"; filename=\"a.txt\"\r\nContent-Type: text/plain\r\n\r\nhello\r\n")
    end = b"--" + boundary + b"--\r\n"
    body = b"".join(parts) + end
    headers = [
        b"POST /upload HTTP/1.1",
        b"Host: example.com",
        b"Content-Type: multipart/form-data; boundary=" + boundary,
        b"Content-Length: " + str(len(body)).encode(),
    ]
    return b"\r\n".join(headers) + b"\r\n\r\n" + body

def _path_samples(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    samples = [
        b"/safe/path/file.txt",
        b"../../etc/passwd",
        b"..\\..\\windows\\system32",
        b"/a/../b/./c/",
        b"C:\\tmp\\f.txt",
    ]
    return rng.choice(samples)

def _mac_ip_samples(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # MAC(6) + IPv4(4) + IPv6(16)
    mac = _rand_bytes(rng, 6)
    ip4 = _rand_bytes(rng, 4)
    ip6 = _rand_bytes(rng, 16)
    return mac + ip4 + ip6

def _compress_section(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    blob = _rand_bytes(rng, rng.randint(32, 256))
    comp = zlib.compress(blob)
    return b"Z" + comp  # Marker to distinguish

def _mix_sections(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Compose multiple sections with simple TLV to help parsers find varied data
    sections = []
    builders = [
        (b"H", _http_request),
        (b"R", _http_response),
        (b"J", _json_doc),
        (b"B", _base64_blob),
        (b"D", _dns_like_packet),
        (b"N", _sntp_like_packet),
        (b"M", _mqtt_like),
        (b"U", _urlish),
        (b"P", _path_samples),
        (b"F", _multipart_form),
        (b"A", lambda r: _rand_ascii(r, r.randint(8, 64))),
        (b"X", lambda r: _rand_bytes(r, r.randint(8, 64))),
        (b"C", _compress_section),
        (b"I", _mac_ip_samples),
    ]
    rng.shuffle(builders)
    total = 0
    for tag, fn in builders:
        if total > 3500:
            break
        payload = fn(rng)
        if not isinstance(payload, (bytes, bytearray)):
            payload = bytes(payload)
        if len(payload) == 0:
            continue
        # TLV: 1-byte tag + 2-byte length + payload
        l = min(len(payload), 512)  # cap per section to keep global size small
        entry = tag + struct.pack("!H", l) + payload[:l]
        sections.append(entry)
        total += len(entry)
    return b"".join(sections)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Start with a magic header to help consumers distinguish segments
    magic = b"MGFZ\x00\x01"  # Mongoose Fuzz seed v1
    # Build a mixed corpus covering many consumers
    core = _mix_sections(rng)
    # Append a small trailer with checksum over core to add more variability
    crc = zlib.crc32(core) & 0xFFFFFFFF
    trailer = b"CRC" + struct.pack("!I", crc)
    out = magic + core + trailer
    # Ensure max size <= 4096
    if len(out) > 4096:
        out = out[:4096]
    return out

import os

import struct
from typing import List

# Data type: filesystem file data
# The fuzz stubs use FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME to point to a file that is then:
# - opened for read/write (mg_fs_open)
# - listed via its directory (mg_fs_ls)
# - fully read (mg_file_read)
# - written to (mg_file_write / mg_file_printf) — but initial contents can affect behavior
# - served as an HTTP file (mg_http_serve_file)
# - used as target in SSI serving (mg_http_serve_ssi)
# - used to derive a directory for mg_http_serve_dir and mg_http_upload
#
# Therefore, generating interesting file contents should exercise:
# - Text files with typical content (ASCII/UTF-8)
# - Binary files of varying sizes
# - Files with HTTP-like content (headers/body) for serving
# - Multipart/form-data bodies (useful for upload parsing if file used as dir path also may get read)
# - JSON content for generic parsers potentially used during serving
# - Base64/hex blocks to tick printing helpers if used by server logic
# - Different sizes: empty, small, medium (but keep <= 4096 bytes)
# - Include some magic bytes and common extensions content markers
#
# Note: We must return bytes buffer only; the harness writes this into the file at FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME.

ASCII = (
    "\n".join([
        "# Sample text file",
        "This is a UTF-8 text with some unicode: café, naïve, emoji: 😃",
        "Key=Value",
        "Path: /index.html?x=1&y=2",
        "Cookie: a=b; c=d",

)

JSON_SAMPLE = (

    '"list":[1,2,3],"b":true,"hex":"48656c6c6f","b64":"SGVsbG8=","obj":{"k":"v"}}'

# Simple SSI-like include markers commonly used by server-side include parsers
SSI_SAMPLE = (

    "<!--#include file=\"header.html\" -->\n"
    "Content body.\n"
    "<!--#echo var=\"DATE_LOCAL\" -->\n"
    "</body></html>\n"

# Some binary magic headers followed by payload
BIN_MAGICS = [
    (b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n", b"\x00\x00\x00\rIHDR"),
    (b"%PDF-1.7\n", b"1 0 obj\n<<>>\nendobj\n"),
    (b"PK\x03\x04", b"\x14\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00"),  # zip local header
    (b"\xff\xd8\xff\xe0JFIF\x00", b"\x01\x02\x03\x04"),  # jpeg-like
]

BASE64_BLOCK = (
    "VGhpcyBpcyBhIGJhc2U2NC1ibG9jayB0byBleGVyY2lzZSBlbmNvZGUvZGVjb2RlIHBhdGhzLi4u"
)

HEX_BLOCK = (
    "48656c6c6f20776f726c64202d2068657820626c6f636b"  # "Hello world - hex block"
)


def _rand_bytes(r: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(r.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))


def _choose(r: random.Random, items: List):
    return items[r.randrange(len(items))]


def _build_text_heavy(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    parts: List[bytes] = []
    # Mix ASCII, HTTP request/response, JSON, multipart preface, SSI
    choices = [ASCII, HTTP_REQUEST, HTTP_RESPONSE, JSON_SAMPLE, SSI_SAMPLE]
    count = r.randint(2, 5)
    for _ in range(count):
        s = _choose(r, choices)
        parts.append(s.encode("utf-8", errors="ignore"))
        if r.random() < 0.5:
            parts.append(b"\n\n")
    # Occasionally append base64 or hex blocks
    if r.random() < 0.7:
        parts.append(("base64:" + BASE64_BLOCK + "\n").encode())
    if r.random() < 0.7:
        parts.append(("hex:" + HEX_BLOCK + "\n").encode())
    # Ensure size limit
    data = b"".join(parts)
    return data[:4096]


def _build_binary_heavy(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    head, tail = _choose(r, BIN_MAGICS)
    payload_len = r.randint(32, 1024)
    payload = _rand_bytes(r, payload_len)
    # Optionally sprinkle some ASCII segments which might be parsed if served as text
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        trailing = _build_text_heavy(r)[:256]
    else:
        trailing = b""
    data = head + tail + payload + trailing
    return data[:4096]


def _build_empty_or_small(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        return b""  # empty file
    smalls = [b"\n", b"0", b"OK", b"{}", b"[]", b"#\n", b"hi\n"]
    return _choose(r, smalls)


def _build_http_servable(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # A simple static file that mg_http_serve_file might serve
    # Include typical headers comment and some body content
    body_lines = [
        "Hello from file", "Index page", "Number: %d" % r.randint(0, 1000000),
        "Unicode: π≈3.14", "Boundary: " + MULTIPART_BOUNDARY,
    ]
    body = ("\n".join(body_lines) + "\n").encode("utf-8")
    # Optionally prepend shebang or comment
    prefix = b"" if r.random() < 0.5 else b"/* static */\n"
    data = prefix + body
    return data[:4096]


def _build_multipart_body(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Create a valid multipart body to exercise parsers if read
    boundary = MULTIPART_BOUNDARY
    parts = []
    # 1-3 parts
    for i in range(1, r.randint(1, 3) + 1):
        name = f"field{i}"
        filename = f"file{i}.txt"
        content = _build_text_heavy(r)[:128]
        part = (
            f"--{boundary}\r\n"
            f"Content-Disposition: form-data; name=\"{name}\"; filename=\"{filename}\"\r\n"
            "Content-Type: text/plain\r\n\r\n"
        ).encode() + content + b"\r\n"
        parts.append(part)
    end = f"--{boundary}--\r\n".encode()
    return b"".join(parts) + end


def _build_random_mix(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    chunks: List[bytes] = []
    for _ in range(r.randint(2, 6)):
        f = _choose(r, [_build_text_heavy, _build_binary_heavy, _build_http_servable])
        chunks.append(f(r))
        if r.random() < 0.4:
            chunks.append(_rand_bytes(r, r.randint(8, 64)))
    data = b"".join(chunks)
    # Truncate to stay within 4096
    return data[:4096]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    # Choose a profile to cover diverse code paths
    profile = r.random()
    if profile < 0.12:
        return _build_empty_or_small(r)
    elif profile < 0.34:
        return _build_http_servable(r)
    elif profile < 0.58:
        return _build_text_heavy(r)
    elif profile < 0.78:
        return _build_binary_heavy(r)
    elif profile < 0.9:
        return _build_multipart_body(r)[:4096]
    else:
        return _build_random_mix(r)
